title: Isolate template expansion before changing encodings
environment: Observed Dify raw-text behavior at that revision. This is not a universal ban on hyphenated IDs or a claim that encoding changes repair interpolation.
goal: Transport encoded input through a workflow template to a receiver.
approach: Historical failed assumption: Transport-symbol interpretation was initially blamed.
what_worked: Historical correction: Use the observed working numeric IDs for HTTP-referenced nodes and verify actual interpolation. Diagnose subsequent authorization failure separately. Verification reported by the source: The next request decoded and reached provider execution; later full smoke succeeded after the independent external-request authorization issue was resolved.
what_failed: Historical observed failure: The receiver rejected the encoded value even though a direct request to the same deployment decoded correctly; changing Base64 to hexadecimal did not fix the workflow path.
why: Confirmed: a reference containing a hyphenated node ID arrived literally rather than expanding. Privacy-safe character-class/length diagnostics distinguished a placeholder from corrupted data.
improved_method: Compare direct receiver and templated-path controls before re-encoding data. Inspect non-sensitive structure to prove expansion without logging payloads or secrets.
when_to_use: Observed Dify raw-text behavior at that revision. This is not a universal ban on hyphenated IDs or a claim that encoding changes repair interpolation.
when_not_to_use: This is not a universal ban on hyphenated IDs or a claim that encoding changes repair interpolation.
known_limitations: This is an independently curated generalization of an earlier recorded failure. No source-side experiment was rerun during this registration; observation_date is the 2026-10-09 knowledge-review date, not the incident date. Applicability and root-cause claims remain limited to the source-reported conditions.
